page.title: A bacterium cuts foreign DNA
page.subtitle: Teaching cartoon · fictional bacterium, generic enzyme · one strand scene driven by the story
page.description: A fictional bacterium recognises a six-letter site on foreign DNA, cuts both backbones and clears the fragments; its own copy of the site carries a cap that blocks binding.

sections.heading: Recognise, bind, cut, clear
text: A classroom cartoon: a short piece of foreign DNA enters a made-up bacterium. A generic restriction enzyme slides along it until a six-letter recognition site matches its pocket, binds, cuts both backbones with a staggered cut and lets go. The two products keep four-letter overhangs before the cell clears them.

The alternate path follows the same enzyme over the bacterium's own copy of the site, where a cap blocks binding. Everything here is authored for teaching; no real organism, enzyme or sequence is depicted and nothing is measured.

initial.caption: Foreign DNA, 24 letters, carries the site at 9–14.
initial.note: The enzyme is free in the cytoplasm. The dashed box marks the six-letter recognition site on both strands. The cap protein nearby matters only on the host's own copy of the site.

steps.text: **Foreign DNA arrives.** A short double strand reaches the bacterium from outside.

scene.caption: The strand arrives; only its first half is in view.

steps.text: **It enters the cell.** The whole strand is now inside, in the same compartment as the enzyme.

scene.caption: The whole strand is inside the cell.
scene.note: Letters 1–24 are visible; the enzyme has not touched the strand yet.

steps.text: **The enzyme scans.** It slides along the backbone, reading letters, until the site's pattern matches its pocket.

scene.caption: The enzyme slides along the strand.
scene.note: Letters it has already passed are dimmed. The site letters stay bright because they are what it is looking for.

steps.text: **Site recognised.** The pocket closes over letters 9–14 on both strands.

scene.caption: It binds at the recognition site.
scene.note: The ring marks the binding event; the site box brightens while the enzyme is bound.

steps.text: **Both backbones are cut.** Upper strand after letter 9, lower strand after letter 13: a staggered cut, so the ends are not flush.

scene.caption: It cuts the upper strand after 9 and the lower after 13.
scene.note: The gap opens between the two cut positions. Each product keeps a four-letter single-stranded overhang.

steps.text: **The products separate.** Product A keeps letters 1–9 over 1–13; product B keeps 10–24 over 14–24.

scene.caption: The two products drift apart.
scene.note: The overhangs are the four letters with no partner: AATT on product B's upper strand and TTAA on product A's lower strand.

steps.text: **The enzyme is released.** It is free again and could cut another copy of the same site.

scene.caption: The enzyme is recycled.
scene.note: Nothing about the enzyme changed; it is ready for the next strand.

steps.text: **Fragments cleared.** The cell degrades the two products; the foreign DNA never got to act.

scene.caption: The cell clears the fragments.
scene.note: The camera closes in on product A as the clean-up starts; product B follows.

steps.text: **Own DNA, same site.** The bacterium's own chromosome carries the same six letters, but a cap sits on them.

scene.caption: The host's own copy of the site carries a cap.
scene.note: On this path the strand stands for the host's own copy: the cap binds the site first and the enzyme scans toward it.

steps.text: **Binding blocked.** The pocket cannot close over the capped letters.

scene.caption: The cap on the host's own copy blocks binding.
scene.note: The enzyme reaches the site but never grips it; no cut event is authored.

steps.text: **Released, strand intact.** The enzyme lets go; the host's DNA is untouched.

scene.caption: The enzyme leaves; the strand is intact.
scene.note: Both backbones remain continuous; compare with the cut path.
